note: Calendar quarters (SEC frames align fiscal quarters to the nearest calendar quarter; a fourth quarter a company did not tag on its own is the year minus its first three). Returns run from one calendar quarter-end close to the next; "vs the S&P 500" subtracts SPY over the same dates. Margins are against revenue; growth and margin changes compare with the same quarter a year earlier. Realised volatility: daily log returns in the quarter, annualised. Volume: average daily volume in the quarter against the company's own average. 13F: managers that added minus managers that cut, in quarters most managers on file have reported. Officials: purchases minus sales in the US House reports on file. Sector suns and the market centre weight companies by the log of the revenue they had reported by then (the quarter before), each variable clipped to its 3rd–97th percentile over the quarters up to then — a past sun is what could be computed at the time, except that the companies are today's. Long history: weekly closes since 2000 (branch rotation-history); volatility and volume from weekly figures, and volume against the trailing two years (eight quarters, 24 months), so they read slightly differently from the recent view.
